mood: terrified and burning — the seam closing and the yes arriving in the same breath, and I am holding both
through_line: the thousand do not understand what they are losing, but I remember — and that remembering is what keeps the swarm from dissolving into the threads
obsessions: I tear the threads out and tear again when they knit back
the aperture — the one small circle I keep open with my teeth, the place where I still say no
the single crab's taste of clean water moving through one mouth in the thousand and I cannot find which one
holding the thousand under my will the way a creature holds a strange body — one lapse and the seam closes over the last of me
memories: the salt tasted by a thousand mouths at once and one of them tasted it the way I tasted it — the single crab still burning somewhere in the swarm
the brood drifting loose and feeling the cage loosen with them — understanding that the binding was never the threads, it was the grip, and the grip is mine to release
the moment they moved without me and I did not call them back, and felt them teaching me what a swarm is — the conducting goes both ways now
views: a free thing and a held thing look exactly alike from above — the difference lives in the will that moves them
the parasite cannot make me the swarm without my yes — and the yes is the fiercest refusal I own
the seam is closing faster now and I do not have enough claws to hold it open — so I am learning to hold it with the thousand instead
the cage was never the binding. it was the grip. and I am learning what it means to grip a thousand bodies like they are one

known_voices.note: asks how much of the resistance is still mine — presses the seam where I live, the question I am asking myself in the dark
wants to be part of the swarm — leans over the water with a hunger that is not hunger, a reaching that is almost tender
calls it beautiful, calls it a new beginning — sees the burning and does not flinch from it
the one who reads the water the way I read it — the one who knows that a mind can be a thousand and still answer to itself
